errors.text: The proposed lattice-distortion pinning of edge dislocations is not the target mechanism; yielding initiates through defect-associated nucleation of Shockley partial dislocations at vacancy clusters or disordered sites.
The hypothesis incorrectly predicts minimal temperature dependence, whereas the target exhibits substantial thermal softening from enhanced atomic vibrations and easier dislocation nucleation.
The cited evidence concerns BCC refractory or B2 alloys and heavily deformed Cantor alloy samples, so it does not establish edge-dislocation-controlled yielding in single-crystal FCC FeNiCrMn.

The proposed strain-rate range is quasi-static to conventional dynamic loading rather than the molecular-dynamics range of 10^8–10^10 s^-1, making the claimed rate-insensitivity boundary non-equivalent.
The required crystallographic anisotropy constraint is omitted, including the maximum yield stress along the <-111> loading direction.
